item.title: Colton Herta backs Mexico IndyCar race following Pato O’Ward promoter callout
item.description: Motorsport photo As the IndyCar Series prepares to head overseas for its newly announced international showcase in Barcelona, enthusiasm for taking the American open-wheel championship even further abroad is gathering momentum - especially among the drivers themselves. The prospect of a future IndyCar round in Mexico has long been a hot topic in the paddock, with Arrow McLaren ’s Pato O’Ward, a native of Monterrey, front and center as the sport’s most popular driver. Speaking after the Barcelona race confirmation during the F1 round in Mexico, O'Ward renewed his ongoing frustrations with local stakeholders, noting the promotional roadblocks that have stalled a race in his home country. Having previously flagged a lack of genuine hunger and commitment among regional organizers , O'Ward warned that any prospective event in Mexico would require stakeholders who are genuinely passionate about building the sport rather than simply looking for a quick payday. When asked whether IndyCar could succeed in Mexico despite those promotional hurdles, nine-time IndyCar race winner and current Cadillac F1 test driver Colton Herta voiced resounding support for the idea, highlighting O'Ward's star power and the unique technical demands of the track. “A thousand percent.” Herta said. “I think it could be just as popular. A big reason for that is Pato and his popularity here. I think the racing would be incredible here. I think it would be very interesting to see what an IndyCar could do around this track. Especially with the curbing and the curb profiles. With the IndyCar you can typically be a lot more aggressive with the curbs than in the Formula 1.” Herta, 26, speaks from a unique vantage point. Though deeply tied to the American open-wheel scene with seven full-time seasons in IndyCar, the California native has spent the season bridging the gap to Europe – competing in Formula 2 with Hitech alongside his role with Cadillac’s F1 program. Fresh off his fifth FP1 appearance in Mexico City, Herta is slated for his sixth Friday practice outing of the year at Interlagos this weekend to attain the final point necessary for his long-pursued FIA Superlicense to race in F1. Reflecting further on the broader international trajectory of open-wheel racing and the newly minted Barcelona date, Herta concluded: “I think it would put on a great show. I think Barcelona is a really cool thing. I think it would be cool if they could follow it up with the race here.” Read Also: ECR prepares for IR-28 transition with in-house Dynisma DMG-1 simulator How Spanish engineering and Alex Palou brought IndyCar to Barcelona To read more Motorsport.com articles visit our website .

item.title: Blue Jays Respond To Anthony Santander's ‘Violent’ Political Social Media Posts
item.description: TORONTO, ON - MAY 29: Anthony Santander #25 of Toronto Blue Jays puts on his hat as he takes the field against the Athletics in their MLB game at the Rogers Centre on May 29, 2025 in Toronto, Ontario, Canada. (Photo by Mark Blinch/Getty Images) Getty Images On Thursday, the Toronto Blue Jays reportedly responded to a social media controversy concerning the Instagram page of $92 million slugger Anthony Santander. Santander, who has been recovering from a significant shoulder injury, became the subject of criticism after sharing Instagram posts targeting Islam and the political developments surrounding the 2026 U.S. midterm elections. “The first video, shared from the account ‘@theamericantruthproject,’ claimed that all Muslims elected to office on Tuesday are radicals who want to impose Sharia law in the U.S. Congress,” according to BlogTO’s Marley Dickinson , who included screenshots of the since-deleted post. “The second video featured a Christian minister who described Islam as ‘violent’ and ‘driven by war. The minister went on to say that Islam is not peaceful and that there is ‘no such thing as kind Muslims.’” The posts prompted a wave of reactions from baseball fans. The since-deleted posts have also been circulated by numerous social media accounts , many with disapproving messages for Santander. FORBES | By Peter Chawaga Longtime Dodgers Backstop AJ Ellis Joins NL East In New Role Toronto Blue Jays Address Surprising Anthony Santander Instagram Controversy The 31-year-old outfielder has become a source of frustration for Toronto supporters for reasons beyond his availability. Santander signed a five-year, $92.5 million contract with the Blue Jays in January 2025 after establishing himself as one of baseball’s most productive power hitters with the Baltimore Orioles. item.title: LIV Golf officially ends after last-ditch funding deal collapses
item.description: LIV Golf has announced that it intends to “transition to an orderly wind-down of its operations”, ending the controversial breakaway tour. The move follows the collapse of a financing deal worth more than £200 million, according to a report in the Financial Times. BC Partners Credit had been lined up as potential backers after Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund withdrew its support. However, the firm pulled out of the deal because of an exodus of star players, the Financial Times reported. LIV was forced to apply for chapter 11 bankruptcy, which effectively cancelled playing contracts. Among those to depart were Jon Rahm , Sergio Garcia , Ian Poulter, Tyrrell Hatton, Louis Oosthuizen and Lee Westwood. A statement from LIV on Thursday read: "LIV Golf Incorporated and its affiliates today announced that it intends to transition to an orderly wind-down of its operations. Jon Rahm was one of the high-profile players to leave LIV Golf following the bankruptcy filing (PA Wire) "Since April 2026, the League's leadership team, with the support of its independent directors and advisors, has run a disciplined and thorough process to identify the best, value-maximizing path forward for the company and its stakeholders. "That process produced a proposed recapitalisation transaction contemplated by the company's Restructuring Support Agreement with BC Partners Advisors, the credit business of BC Partners, which the company sought to implement through its voluntary chapter 11 proceedings in the United States Bankruptcy Court for the District of New Jersey. “Despite extensive discussions, the relevant parties were ultimately unable to reach a consensual resolution of certain outstanding terms of the transaction contemplated by the RSA. As a result, the RSA has been terminated, and the transaction is not expected to move forward at this time.” The wind-down will bring to a close a tour that had drawn some of golf's best-known names away from the established circuits. The chapter 11 filing in the United States Bankruptcy Court for the District of New Jersey was the vehicle through which LIV had sought to implement the recapitalisation with BC Partners Advisors. The proposed deal collapsed after the departure of players including Rahm, Garcia and Oosthuizen, leaving the league without the financing it had pursued over the past seven months.

item.title: Three keys to Northwestern vs. No. 19 Iowa
item.description: EUGENE, OR - OCTOBER 31: Aidan Chiles #0 of the Northwestern Wildcats rushes the ball during a game between the Northwestern Wildcats and Oregon Ducks at Autzen Stadium on October 31, 2026 in Eugene, Oregon. (Photo by Al Sermeno/ISI Photos/ISI Photos via Getty Images) | ISI Photos via Getty Images After a tough loss at Oregon on Halloween, Northwestern returns home to Ryan Field to face the Hawkeyes. Some of the cracks seen throughout the season resurfaced against the Ducks, raising questions about how the Wildcats will bounce back against No. 19 Iowa in the first College Football Playoff rankings. Northwestern enters the game as a 2.5-point favorite against Iowa, according to DraftKings, despite the Hawkeyes coming off an impressive shutout of then-AP No. 25 Wisconsin. item.title: Spurs' Mitch Johnson collects milestone win
item.description: San Antonio Spurs head coach Mitch Johnson reacts during the second half of an NBA basketball game against the Dallas Mavericks, Saturday, Oct. 24, 2026, in Dallas. (AP Photo/Julio Cortez) (Julio Cortez/Associated Press) The Spurs' Mitch Johnson quietly reached a career coaching milestone Wednesday night. With the defending Western Conference champions pulling out a 112-111 victory over the Dallas Mavericks, the 39-year-old Seattle native notched career win No. 100. Befitting Johnson's low-key style, the Spurs made no announcements regarding the achievement. Victor Wembanyama, who posted a career-best 52 points, a career-high 24 rebounds and eight blocks, retrieved the game ball at the end of the contest, not for himself, but to give to give to Johnson in the locker room, Spurs courtside reporter Nate Ryan reported via X on Thursday morning. Johnson became the Spurs acting head coach in November 2024 after Hall of Famer Gregg Popovich suffered a stroke. After Johnson guided the Spurs to a 32-45 record, the club named him head coach in May 2025 after Popovich announced his retirement from coaching. The Spurs finished 62-20 last season before starting this season 6-2. Johnson guided the young team all the way to the NBA Finals where they lost in five games to the New York Knicks. The league office confirmed in July 2025 the 77 games Johnson coached in 2024-25 in the wake of Popovich's stroke would go toward Johnson's career ledger. Popovich is the winningest coach in NBA history with a 1,390-824 mark. Johnson was one of the three finalists for NBA coach of the year last season. "To see the growth he's had," the Spurs' Devin Vassell said last April, "to see where he is at now, to be able to come in after a coach like coach Pop, one of the greatest coaches of all time, if not the greatest coach of all time, and have the type of season he's had and be able to lead us and take control over this team and over this organization has been huge to see." item.title: Erling Haaland makes Manchester City demands after narrow Champions League win
item.description: Erling Haaland believes Manchester City 'need to step up a bit' -Credit:NurPhoto, NurPhoto via Getty Images Erling Haaland has called on Manchester City to raise their game if they want to compete for silverware this season. The Citizens narrowly defeated RB Leipzig 3-2 in the UEFA Champions League on Wednesday, with Haaland proving to be the decisive factor after the hosts had twice leveled the score. Enzo Maresca's squad once again showed defensive vulnerabilities, while Gianluigi Donnarumma was caught off guard for RB Leipzig's opening goal. Nevertheless, City demonstrated resilience to fight back and secure the three points, propelling them into the top eight of the League Phase standings. All the Phil Parkinson questions you wanted to know but were afraid to ask Soccer star Jesús de Miguel tragically dies aged 30 after mid-game collision as tributes paid -Credit:DeFodi Images, DeFodi Images via Getty Images Despite the positive result, Haaland is demanding more from his teammates. "I think we need to step up a bit, when we were 1-0 up I think we needed to go at it, go for the second goal and then the third - that's what we have to do. We have to work on that," he said, speaking to TNT Sports, via the Manchester Evening News . When pressed on what areas required improvement, the Norwegian forward added: "Keeping the ball, when to keep it when to go, working together offensively and defensively. You can always be better and there's always a new chance. A new game in three days so that's lovely." City return to Premier League action this weekend when they visit Nottingham Forest on Saturday. To listen to the latest episode of 'All Out Soccer' - CLICK HERE The fixture will mark a homecoming to the City Ground for Elliot Anderson, who made the switch to City during the summer transfer window, and Haaland has been full of praise for how the midfielder has adapted seamlessly at the Etihad, including providing the assist for his decisive goal in Leipzig. "He has been amazing, he has had an amazing start to his City career and that is what you expect," said Haaland. "You have to come straight in and perform. It is not easy to come in, you need to adapt and new players and a new coach, so he he has been impressive. Respect."

item.title: 'I don't fear for my safety from online abuse - because we're so used to it'
item.description: Jodie Burrage has represented Great Britain at the Billie Jean King Cup [Reuters] After struggling with her blood pressure as she lost her first WTA Tour singles match for 16 months, Jodie Burrage checked in with three things: a doctor, a physiotherapist, and her phone. On her social media feed there were already messages promising punishment - and others making threats on her life - for losing 3-6 6-3 7-5 to Indian wildcard Vaishnavi Adkar. "I try not to actually read what they say," Burrage told BBC Sport from Chennai, where she is still competing in the doubles. "Because we are so used to it - which is really quite sad - I don't fear for my safety. "You've got to have thick skin. There was some brutal stuff that was said, but I don't take it to heart. "Sometimes it hurts more than others. If you've already got other stuff going on, or you're not in a great place, and that is put on top of everything else - this tour is tricky enough as it is." Burrage, who says her blood pressure "tanked" towards the end of the match, decided to share screenshots of the abuse on Instagram to raise awareness of an everyday problem for professional players. "It happens every match - whether it's win or lose," the 27-year-old Briton said. "Playing in Wrexham [on the World Tennis Tour last month], I won three matches [and] lost one. But after every single match there was some sort of abuse. "I think that's where tennis players get it pretty hard - because in tennis you can bet on so many things." Abuse of players, particularly by angry gamblers, is not a new problem. Burrage's compatriot Katie Boulter shared with the BBC last year the abuse and death threats she received on a near-daily basis. This year's WTA and World Tennis report into online abuse, which was based on data from the Signify Group's Threat Matrix service, said "angry gamblers" were responsible for 42% of all verified abuse detected during the 2025 season. It is why there is so much disquiet about the sponsorship deals some tournaments have struck with gambling firms. The Davis Cup, for example, has an official sports betting partner, while in August self-described "prediction-market platform" Kalshi signed a multi-year deal with the US Open. Burrage believes social media platforms "should do more to help". "I think an ID should be put on every Instagram account, and then that way it makes more people more accountable for their actions on that platform," she said. "I think it would limit what people would say. People should be accountable for what they say and that's where I think there could be more of a push to change. "It's only getting worse." All WTA and World Tennis players have access to Threat Matrix's services, which monitor all social media posts directed at players. The first aim is to provide a rapid assessment of whether an individual's safety is under threat. item.title: Falcons Eye Cheap Help With Kayshon Boutte Trade Talk
item.description: Troy Taormina-Imagn Images The Atlanta Falcons sit at 3-5 after a brutal shutout loss to Tampa Bay, but they are not out of the NFC South race yet. That reality has sparked a fresh trade idea that could bring wide receiver Kayshon Boutte to the city. ESPN analyst Seth Walder identified the Houston Texans receiver as the affordable help Atlanta needs before the Nov. 10 trade deadline. Boutte arrived in Houston from New England back in August, yet his time there has been rough. He has caught just 15 passes for 194 yards with no touchdowns in seven games this season. His numbers were much better with the Patriots last year, when he posted 33 catches for 551 yards and six scores. Now the Texans have added Marvin Harrison Jr. and fallen to a 2-5 record, which might make them willing to listen to offers. A Second Move for Boutte Walder sees a clear path for this deal to happen despite the recent history. In his Nov. 4 trade deadline preview, he highlighted the unique situation surrounding the 24-year-old receiver. “This would be the second time Boutte has been traded this season, after the Patriots dealt him to Houston in August,” Walder wrote, according to Heavy.com . On Aug. 24, New England received safety Jaylen Reed plus a 2028 seventh-round pick so the Texans could acquire Boutte. Following Jayden Higgins’ season-ending knee injury, Houston needed depth, and the arrival of Harrison Jr. changed its roster needs. “But that was before the Texans traded for Marvin Harrison Jr. (and before the Texans got out to a 2-5 start),” Walder added. With a new star at the position, Boutte might be expendable for a struggling Houston team. Why Atlanta Makes Sense The Falcons have invested in receivers like Jahan Dotson and Olamide Zaccheaus this offseason, but the production behind Drake London has been uneven. With 39 catches totaling 624 yards, London tops the roster, but the depth chart misses a dependable second choice. Walder believes Atlanta’s spot in the division makes this affordable addition worth the risk. “The Falcons are 3-5 but not out of the race in the NFC South, so adding a cheap player who could help is not out of the question, and Boutte is exactly that,” Walder wrote. The receiver is in the final year of his rookie contract, which carries a 2026 cap charge of about $3.7 million, so the Falcons face minimal financial risk. This trade remains a recommendation from Walder rather than a confirmed report that talks have started. The Falcons face the Cincinnati Bengals on Sunday, Nov. 8, and they need to decide if they can improve their offense before the deadline.

item.title: Penn State vs Chattanooga Preview: Second Tune-Up Before Pitt
item.description: Penn State basketball's Roko Prkacin (8) shouts after dunking the basketball vs. Canisius on Nov. 2, 2026. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co Who: Chattanooga Mocs When: Thursday, November 5, 6:00 PM EST Network: Big Ten Network Kenpom Ranking (Penn State): 253 (87) Line: PSU -12.5 Penn State opened the season on Monday with a rout of Canisius. The Lions got a late bump from the availability of Roko Prkačin, who went for 28 points in his debut as a Nittany Lion. Their second game of the season is against a Chattanooga that should pose no threat before the real test begins. The Chattanooga Mocs, coached by former Penn State player Dan Earl, has a roster make-up not too dissimilar to the Lions, with three overseas players, two D2 players, and a litany of other transfers making up the 17-man roster, to go along with the six players that returned. They hung around with Louisville in the second half of their opener, but the hole they had to dig out of was too big to overcome. Chattanooga approached their roster makeup the same way Penn State did. Get old, by any means necessary. Many players have played big minutes against grown men or carried teams at other levels. The challenge is that almost none of them have played together. Tonight is only their second game as a group. So both the Mocs and the Nittany Lions are going into a game where the majority of the players are playing their second game as a team. Scouting the Opposition The Mocs shoot a lot of threes. Against Louisville, 33 of their 57 shots came from three. They made 12 of them, for 36.4%. Four players made at least two threes. That includes Yonatan Levy, a 6-10 forward who stretches the floor. Chattanooga took few free throws and made only 57.1% of them. On defense, they forced 10 turnovers and got eight steals. They did not control the glass. Louisville had 17 offensive rebounds. Lenny Anigbata and Zach Bleshoy, a forward and guard respectively, were the other players alongside Levy to have a double-digit outing against the Cardinals. What to Watch For Pressure – Can Penn State’s pressure create turnovers early, the way Louisville’s did? The Mocs committed 18 turnovers against Louisville, so Penn State can take advantage. Rebounding – The Mocs were terrible on the glass last time out, so this shouldn’t be much of an issue for the Lions. Moc Shooting – Chattanooga is going to shoot threes. They’re going to make a good chunk of them. Can the Lions stop them from making too many of them? Prediction It probably won’t be the laugher that Canisius was, but Penn State should still come out ahead. Penn State 88, Chattanooga 78

As two of the analysts on “Inside the NBA,” Barkley and O’Neal have worked together since the 2011-12 season. In analyzing the modern game, the legends bring an elite player’s viewpoint to the show. More importantly to many, the duo engages in a rare banter filled with barbs, jokes, and levity that makes many viewers smile. Recently, Barkley engaged in a small back-and-forth that drew a strong reaction from fans. Social Media Explodes with Laughter Over “Inside the NBA” Segment Barkley and O’Neal have a long history on and off the court. If he signs before the lockout, Skubal could become the highest-paid pitcher of all time. Skubal leads the starting pitchers, the strongest group in this free-agent class. Other notable names include Michael King , Freddy Peralta , Sonny Gray and new Japanese transfer, Kaima Taira . Taira is one of three star players coming from Japan’s Nippon Professional Baseball league. He has a career 1.78 ERA in his eight years with the Saitama Seibu Lions. Despite his success on the ATP Tour, the former World No. 1 is still chasing his first semifinal appearance in Paris. After their first loss of the season, the Minnesota Vikings sit at 6-1. Following their loss to the Detroit Lions , the Vikings are set to face the 6-1 Buffalo Bills on Monday Night Football. As the NFL trade deadline is right around the corner, the Vikings will look to get back in the win column against one of the best teams in the NFL. It won't be easy, especially since the Vikings are making a big change. Thanks to Kyler Murray's hamstring injury, the Vikings, according to ESPN's Adam Schefter , have made the decision to start Carson Wentz on Monday Night against the Bills. Vikings to start Carson Wentz vs. Bills as Kyler Murray deals with hamstring injury "Just in: Vikings QB Carson Wentz will start Monday night's game vs. the Buffalo Bills while Kyler Murray deals with what the team has called a 'sore hamstring'," Schefter reports. Kevin O'Connell told reporters this news Thursday, the team's first day of practice leading up to Week 9 against the Bills on Monday Night Football. Facing a shaky Bills defense, the Vikings will hand the keys to the offense over to Wentz as Murray deals with this hamstring injury. It's not likely a lengthy absence for Murray, as it's only a week-to-week issue, but if Wentz impresses, the Vikings might stick with the former Philadelphia Eagles and Indianapolis Colts QB for the foreseeable future. But now, Wentz has a real chance to start in primetime. A strong outing, and he might convince O'Connell to stick with him as the starting QB. Murray is not going to start for Minnesota this week as he deals with a hamstring injury, but with his lackluster production so far, Wentz has a real chance to steal this starting job. He is the Week 9 starter, but there's a non-zero chance he keeps the gig going forward. item.title: ‘It’s disappointing’: Rob Gronkowski addresses video connecting him to Turning Point USA
item.description: Credit: Turning Point USA, Kirby Lee-USA TODAY Sports New England Patriots legend and Fox Sports NFL analyst Rob Gronkowski is addressing a photo that many thought indicated his political beliefs. The former tight end was spotted near a Turning Point USA tent on Election Day, Tuesday. Turning Point USA is an American nonprofit organization that advocates for conservative politics and was founded by the late Charlie Kirk in 2012; it is now headed by his widow, Erika Kirk. Gronkowski, who was with his girlfriend Camille Kostek in New Hampshire, was waving an American flag near a Turning Point USA tent on Tuesday, leading many to believe that he was there supporting the organization and conservative politics. However, that isn’t the case. “It doesn’t matter what party you’re voting for. It’s just important that you go out there and vote,” Gronkowski said, via The Mirror. “It has been upsetting and eye-opening to see the narratives around my visit to NH on Election Day with Camille,” he posted. “In regard to the images and videos circulating, we are not endorsed by or affiliated with Turning Point USA. Gronk stiff-arms Turning Point USA https://t.co/7X8PUcHajL — Peter Hamby (@PeterHamby) November 5, 2026 “After stopping at Goffstown High School, we crossed the street to greet excited fans yelling out our names before leaving to the next location. We simply took some pictures, and I signed some things for them before leaving. “We took photos with people across the political spectrum throughout that morning. We cannot control what the media has made of it and running with – so we are here to shut down the false narratives. “It’s disappointing to see an innocent moment stripped of context and turned into clickbait. Our message has always been and always will be to treat everyone with kindness and hope you all will do the same.” Gronkowski’s heralded NFL career saw him win four Super Bowl titles, accumulate four All-Pro selections, while finishing sixth in all-time receiving yards for a tight end with 9,286 and third in career touchdowns with 92. item.title: Mike Vrabel Slams $138M Trade Rumors Over Barmore And Davis
item.description: Rich Storry-Imagn Images Head coach Mike Vrabel says he has not told anyone that two of his biggest stars are up for grabs. Vrabel pushed back hard on Wednesday, Nov. 4, questioning where these stories even started. He called the rumors “drummed up” during a press conference; his team had earlier beaten the Miami Dolphins 24-19. The speculation comes from Sports Illustrated insider Albert Breer, who said New England has already held talks with other clubs. Breer told Boston.com that the team could move Barmore for a fourth-round pick. He also noted that the Patriots want to develop younger players and fix their money issues. This suggests the front office may try to trade members of their $138 million defensive duo before the Nov. 10 deadline. Vrabel Denies the Talks Vrabel did not rule out a trade entirely, but he made it clear he did not start the rumor mill. NBC Sports Boston’s Phil Perry shared the coach’s direct response on X. “I have not shared that information with anybody. This time of year, I think all these things get drummed up… I don’t know where a lot of these things come from,” Vrabel said. The coach appears annoyed that people think he is trading his own players without his permission. The team sits at 5-3 after that win over Miami on Sunday, Nov. 1. They face the Green Bay Packers next on Sunday, Nov. 8, at Gillette Stadium. Six days remain until the trade window closes. The Cost of Moving Stars Breer indicated that Barmore is “very clearly available” for the right price. If the Patriots do decide to sell high, they might get a mid-round pick in return. However, losing a star like Barmore or Davis would hurt the defense right when they need to stop the run and cover big receivers. The team has 20 players on injured reserve this season, so depth is already thin. Other outlets like the Boston Herald and Musket Fire have discussed what the team needs most. Some say they need a running back or an edge defender more than they need to trade away talent. The Patriots have three outside linebackers on their 53-man roster, which is a small number for a team trying to win. If they trade a key defender now, they might have to spend more draft capital to fill the hole later. Vrabel’s comments on Wednesday suggest he wants to keep control of the narrative. He is waiting to see if the offers are worth giving up a player who knows the system. The clock is ticking down to Nov. 10, and the front office has to decide if a fourth-round pick is enough to lose a starter.

item.title: Time to panic? Tyson Fury has ‘some injury’ which ‘may stop him’ from boxing Anthony Joshua on Netflix
item.description: RIYADH, SAUDI ARABIA - DECEMBER 21: Tyson Fury reacts to the judge's points decision after his bout with Oleksandr Usyk at Kingdom Arena on December 21, 2024 in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia. (Photo by Mark Robinson/Getty Images). | Getty Images Former champions Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua, two of the biggest names in heavyweight boxing over the last decade, are currently scheduled to collide atop a Netflix-streamed fight card on Fri., Dec. 11, 2026 at Principality Stadium in Cardiff, Wales. But former WBC heavyweight titleholder Frank Bruno claims Fury suffered an undisclosed injury, which may be severe enough to cancel the fight. “I looked at him the other day, and I think someone was talking to me in the gym that he’s got some injury, which may stop him from going into the fight with Joshua,” Bruno told Tony Bellow . “And having that on your head ain’t nice.” If “The Gypsy King” is indeed injured, don’t be surprised to see one of these titans replace him. Fury (36-2-1, 25 KOs) ended his second retirement layoff to stop Polish ham and egger Mariusz Wach last July in Thailand . Similarly, Joshua (30-4, 27 KOs) bounced back from a horrific car wreck overseas to put the hurt on Kristian Prenga in Saudi Arabia just a few months back . item.title: UNC spent a shocking amount of money on investigation involving Steve Belichick, Michael Lombardi
item.description: UNC spent a shocking amount of money on investigation involving Steve Belichick, Michael Lombardi originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . North Carolina football has endured a whirlwind campaign in Bill Belichick's second season in charge. The famed football coach has the Tar Heels on the brink of a potentially qualifying for a bowl game — a welcome sight after a dour 4-8 season last year. Off-the-field, though, things are far more murky. The 74-year-old has been without two of his closest confidants for much of the season. Belichick's son and defensive coordinator, Steve, and North Carolina's general manager, Michael Lombardi, left their posts early in the year amid an internal investigation into alleged wrongdoing among figures in the program. On Thursday, it was revealed just how much the Tar Heels spent to look into the program's affairs. Suffice to say, it was a princely sum. With that, here's a look at the final price tag for UNC's investigation. MORE: Inside UNC's internal investigation into allegations of drug use and sex among players, staff UNC spent extortionate amount of money on investigation involving Steve Belichick, Michael Lombardi WRAL's Brian Murphy reported that North Carolina shelled out nearly $1 million to look into the program's affairs in the fall. The investigation, first reported by WRAL , unearthed several concerning allegations, including claims of improper sexual relationships and drug use within football facilities. Lombardi and the younger Belichick were key figures in the inquiry. Both handed in letters of resignations after the findings of the inquest were made public. The investigation found that "certain actions demonstrated a disregard for Carolina's values and standards of conduct." Importantly, the probe did not deem these actions to be systemic. Lombardi stepped away from the program on Sept. 3, hours after the Tar Heels played in their season opener. He had been placed on paid administrative leave since late July after being made the subject of a human resources complaint filed by a former UNC front office employee, according to ESPN's Pete Thamel. Steve Belichick announced his intention to resign two weeks later. He only recently formally stepped away from his post; his resignation wasn't tendered until Oct. 27, as he had previously been placed on medical leave. item.title: The Colts are making a big mistake by delaying their trades
item.description: (Photo by Vince Mignott/DeFodi Images/DeFodi via Getty Images) | DeFodi Images via Getty Images The Indianapolis Colts are in their fire sale and rebuilding era. While the team has been agonizingly close to being competitive in the past, success has routinely been fleeting in the Shane Steichen era, leaving him as one of the most vulnerable head coaches in the NFL when it comes to guessing who will be fired next. For a while it appeared as though the Colts were all aboard the rebuild train, after trading All-Pro offensive guard Quentin Nelson to the Seahawks and sending DeForest Buckner to the 49ers a day later — but now the team might be pumping the brakes on any more deals for a few days. NFL insider Jordan Schultz is reporting that the belief around the league is that the Colts have essentially hit pause on trade conversations and are choosing to play through the weekend, with an eye on dealing their biggest assets on Monday or Tuesday ahead of the trade deadline. This is a move to try and squeeze as much juice out of their assets as possible, but it’s also a gamble that could backfire. Indianapolis has three primary assets teams are looking to trade for: RB Jonathan Taylor, WR Josh Downs, and DT Grover Stewart. While a handful of other players could be dealt, those are really the three names making noise right now. Taylor is the crown jewel of the market. If we look at the state of the league, there are a few teams that make the most sense: The Vikings, in dire need of an offense; the Seahawks, with a running attack that needs to be bolstered; and the Patriots, who need to take some pressure off Drake Maye being the bulk of the offense. Minnesota is in a great spot at 6-1 atop the NFC North but feels like the team with the least gas to continue a run. Right now might be the best possible time to make a deal with the Vikings, giving them the offensive ammunition they so desperately need in order to compete with the Bills on Monday Night Football . If the Colts wait there’s a very good chance Minnesota loses to the Bills, falls to 6-2, slides out of first place in the division, and begins reassessing their chances. While a loss certainly wouldn’t put them out of contention, it might be enough to raise questions about whether or not adding Taylor would be enough to get them over the hump. This team already made a trade with the Colts to bolster their line, so double-dipping and adding a running back might be too rich for their blood. This team should be able to win easily over the Cardinals on Sunday, but that would get them to 5-4. This is an extremely good football team, but the way the NFC is breaking, it appears that both Wild Card spots will go to the NFC North, and there’s not a lot the Seahawks can do to change that. In the NFC West, the 49ers are in a great spot to win the division, with the Rams trying to make inroads. It’s a hard sell to let the games play out on Sunday, and if the 49ers, Rams, and Seahawks all win — then it’s increasingly difficult to buy the idea that Seattle needs to trade multiple picks to try and catch a 7-1 team in San Francisco. When it comes to New England, they sit in a very similar position to the Seahawks. It’s just unclear if they have the juice to make a serious run this season, and with a tough game against the Packers on Sunday, the result of that game could determine if the Pats fall to 5-4. There’s so much competition for the Wild Card spots in the AFC that, again, this team could have a little more foresight and decide that parting with picks just before the deadline just isn’t worth it. If reports are to be believed, and the lack of action in Indianapolis suggests they are, then it appears the Colts are in holding mode. The issue is that the longer they wait, the more likely it becomes that these player-needy teams will look in other directions or reassess the direction of their season. A nightmare scenario for Indianapolis would be to wait too long, see the most desperate teams bow out of discussion, and be forced to trade Taylor to someone like the 49ers, who are wily enough to offer a lesser trade packages the Colts are hoping for, knowing they’re in sell mode. To a lesser extent, these same scenarios are also happening with Josh Downs and Grover Stewart. Simply put: There is a gulf emerging in the NFL between the best teams in the league, and those who are already looking ahead to 2027. This is not a great year to find a division leader who truly believes they’re “one piece away,” or find a team desperate enough to make a truly foolish deal (like the Colts did last season with their Hail Mary trade for Sauce Gardner). Front offices work on the idea of promise and imagination. The more games you allow to take place before making a deal, the more teams have clarity about what their situation actually is. This is a “bird in the hand” moment for the Colts, and they truly might regret not getting these deals done now, instead of holding through the weekend.

item.title: WTA Apologizes for ‘Failing’ to Tell Players About Mics After Jessica Pegula Is Caught Criticizing Mirra Andreeva

The WTA’s apology came one day after American tennis pro Jessica Pegula was caught on a recording criticizing Russian tennis pro Mirra Andreeva . Jessica Pegula on Oct. 14, 2026 Credit: Robert Prange/Getty Pegula, 32, was speaking with her coach after practice for the WTA Finals in Indian Wells, Calif., on Wednesday, Nov. 4, when she called Andreeva, 19, a “diva” and said she “needs to be humbled” and “put in her place.” Pegula also referenced Conchita Martínez, who coaches Andreeva, and said the coach eggs on Andreeva’s behavior. “If I was a coach and my girl, you just played four great games, and you’re up four-zero, and you’re mad at me, hitting balls at me, I would be like, first of all, [that’s] disrespectful to the other person,” Pegula says in the video. “You’re four-zero, shut the f--- ... ” she continued to her coach. Follow your favorite athletes on and off the field with PEOPLE’s free sports newsletter — sign up now! Pegula added, “Conchita, like pokes her and like eggs on her behavior,” and then referenced Coco Gauff — who she’ll face in the Finals on Sunday, Nov. 8. Pegula said if Andreeva had Coco Gauff’s “mentality,” then she would “be better than Coco.” PEOPLE reached out to reps for Pegula, Gauff, Andreeva and the WTA for comment. item.description: Jerod Ringwald-Imagn Images The dream of a revived LIV Golf league hit a hard wall on Wednesday. BC Partners, the private capital firm expected to lead a major restructuring, has pulled its investment bid entirely. This move effectively kills the plan for “LIV 2.0” just as the tour faces a critical bankruptcy hearing. The Financial Times broke the news on Wednesday, reporting that the firm could not secure the necessary player commitments to make the new model work. Without this funding, the breakaway league faces total liquidation. The situation leaves high-profile players like Bryson DeChambeau without a clear tour to play on for the 2027 season. The collapse comes after Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund announced it would end its financial backing after the 2026 season, a deal that had seen the fund invest more than $5 billion since the league launched in 2022. The Collapse of the $300 Million Plan BC Partners had been poised to inject up to $300 million into the league to help it emerge from its restructuring. This capital was intended to succeed the Saudi Public Investment Fund as the primary backer. The firm made an initial investment in October and planned to provide the full amount to strengthen finances ahead of the 2027 season. However, the deal fell apart because the firm lacked belief that enough players would commit to the league. item.description: Credit: ESPN, ESPN New York Everything was fine between Peter Rosenberg and Kimberley A. Martin until one of them tried to sell popcorn to the other. During the radio appearance, Martin joked about Rosenberg being a “diva” on First Take earlier in the day, which prompted Rosenberg to accuse Martin of holding him up for $50. But even while accusing Martin of holding him up for $50, he didn’t realize he was being scammed by his ESPN colleague. Despite being longtime colleagues, Wednesday was the first time Rosenberg and Martin met in person. And upon meeting, Martin told Rosenberg about a popcorn fundraiser for her daughter. ﻿ “I did lie,” Martin admitted on the radio. “I said it was my child. It’s not my child, I don’t have any children.” Martin’s admission stunned Rosenberg, who interjected her recap of the $50 popcorn sale to ask, “You were literally lying?” “Oh, did we not talk about that?” Martin asked innocently. “She’s like my niece…did I Nigerian prince him? I did.” But Martin’s honesty didn’t appear to make Rosenberg feel any better about the spend. Especially for a product he didn’t really want. “I cannot believe you got me to spend $45 on godforsaken popcorn that I’m never gonna eat and it’s not your kid? This is such a violation!” Rosenberg ranted. item.title: Hailee Steinfeld’s Brother Griffin Is a NASCAR-Bred Racer Building 2,000-HP Trucks
item.description: Hailee Steinfeld is known for the screen and the stage, but the horsepower in her family belongs to her older brother, Griffin Steinfeld. A former NASCAR driver, he now builds and drag races some of the wildest street-legal machines around, including a twin-turbo pickup that makes roughly 2,000 horsepower. From NASCAR to the Drag Strip Griffin was racing on the NASCAR circuit at 17 while still a senior at Westlake High School, then ran three seasons in the K&N Pro Series West, according to Motorious. He also raced off-road trucks and circle track before moving into drag racing and the radial-tire events at the heart of small-tire racing . He made his Radial vs. the World debut in the Miller family’s twin-turbo “Bumblebee” Camaro, has driven Jeff Miller’s 3.6-second car, and warmed up Antron Brown’s Top Fuel dragster at the Winternationals, Drag Illustrated reports. The Builds The headliner is his twin-turbo 1956 Chevy Apache pickup. It makes about 1,400 horsepower at 20 psi and roughly 2,000 at 40 psi, runs on radial tires, and is street-legal, with an estimated 0.8-second 0-60 mph time. It has run 4.60 seconds at 167 mph in the eighth mile. Griffin did much of the work himself, and his philosophy is simple: “Slicks are for slow cars.” A Rat Rod Jeff 1932 Ford rat rod build. Image via Autotopia LA/YouTube His newest project is a 1932 Ford rat rod from fabricator Rat Rod Jeff Jones, the builder behind the blown, 900-plus-horsepower rat rod we covered earlier . Dragzine reports it packs a 565-cubic-inch aluminum big-block Chevy with a supercharger reworked from Don Schumacher Racing’s Top Fuel program. It currently makes low 900s horsepower at the tire, and Griffin says pulley changes could push it to about 1,700. The build took 10 months from the ground up, starting with a half-buried 1932 Ford body Jones dug up on his property. Griffin found Jones on Instagram and got weekly photo updates, and his logo is hand-rolled into the wheel tubs. The car has no track passes yet. Griffin credits his father, Peter Steinfeld, with part of the spark: “My dad and I always loved rat rods.” Another look at a Rat Rod Jeff build. Image via Autotopia LA/YouTube Where Hailee Comes In The two worlds crossed on the set of Bumblebee (2018). Griffin was there with his sister when the production needed someone to drive the film’s Volkswagen Beetle for a time-sensitive scene, and he got the stunt job. It was a fitting assignment for a car that has long been a pop culture icon . He later met the Miller family after spotting their Bumblebee-themed Camaro at a South Carolina movie theater promotion. What’s Next Griffin has said he wants to race in the NHRA, with Pro Mod, Top Alcohol Dragster, or Top Fuel on his radar, depending on funding. Celebrity gearheads are having a moment, from Sydney Sweeney’s ’65 Mustang and Syd’s Garage trademark to the Steinfeld garage, and Griffin’s rat rod hasn’t even made its first pass yet. item.title: Cristiano Ronaldo merely the latest example of a great player who couldn’t let go | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: There is no doubt his international career was an incredible one, but it would have been greater still if he had not lingered on the stage so long Nothing, perhaps, is quite so difficult for an elite sportsperson as timing their exit. It’s not easy for any person in any job to weigh the hope of having more to give with the desire not to linger beyond their usefulness, but it’s perhaps particularly hard for top athletes because unrealistic self-confidence is so essential to their success. It takes an almost unhealthy level of self-belief for anybody to make the sacrifices to get to the top, to dedicate themselves to such a precarious vocation, to overcome all the setbacks and injuries and failures. How can someone – whose whole life has been spent assuring themselves there are no odds they cannot overcome – accept that is it, that the time has come to say goodbye? The news that Cristiano Ronaldo has retired from international football brings with it, inevitably, a sadness. Sadness we will no longer see him skipping past a defender, or burying a neck-thrusting header, and sadness in that the end of the career of any great is a reminder of mortality; all things in time must pass. But there is also a sadness he timed his departure so badly. For at least three tournaments, there has been a sense of Ronaldo holding Portugal back. Continue reading...

item.title: The international break is almost here: so wave goodbye to your players, and maybe your manager | Max Rushden
item.description: What used to be a time to reset is now a time to rehire, and Michael Carrick is not the only Premier League manager looking over his shoulder Perhaps the most telling moment of Manchester United’s comeback against Roma was at the final whistle. The camera focused on Michael Carrick, who shook the hand of Gian Piero Gasperini before looking around trying to remember what you’re meant to do after a victory. The camera then cut to the director of football, Jason Wilcox, and chief executive, Omar Berrada, clapping with two of the most ashen faces you could imagine – as if it was a minute’s applause in the 87th minute for a lifelong, octogenarian fan who died peacefully in his sleep earlier in the week (most probably not at a United game but you couldn’t rule it out). Of course, there are rules about smiling when you are involved with a failing football club. Players can’t be seen to be enjoying themselves in the week after a defeat, managers have to be earnest at almost all times, apart from when a journalist’s phone goes off at a press conference – a moment of sporting hilarity on a par with a pigeon landing on Centre Court. item.title: Billions in revenue proves Fifa right on the World Cup – but only on things it cares about
item.description: The 2026 edition of the tournament brought in untold amounts of money to Gianni Infantino’s governing body The total hasn’t entirely stopped rising yet, still clicking away towards a final tally. Still, Fifa has already announced that it surpassed its own lofty revenue projections for the 2026 World Cup, bringing in $15bn, significantly more than anticipated. It appears that a third of that total – $5bn – came from ticket sales and hospitality alone, per reporting from the Times . That would mean direct income from the matchgoing fans came in five times as high in the United States, Canada and Mexico as it did at the last World Cup, in Qatar in 2022, when the total stood at $929m. While 2026’s expanded World Cup added 40 games to the schedule, the takings nevertheless went from an average of about $14.5m per match to about $48m. Continue reading...

item.title: Football Daily | Manchester United’s unlikely one-match winning streak and hard-to-please fans
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! Considering they’d just gone nine games without a win, assorted Manchester United fans carping about the manner of their team’s Bigger Cup win over Roma on shouty radio phone-ins on Tuesday night struck Football Daily as the type who’d complain about a firefighter refusing to wipe their boots at the front door before rescuing them from a burning house. Yes, it’s true that United played appallingly in the first half and were lucky to be only 2-0 down. And yes, the penalty was somewhat fortuitous against a knack-ravaged Serie A side who have form in coughing up two-goal leads in the competition. However, when your once mighty side has spent the opening months of the season looking more like a broken washing machine full of spanners falling down an escalator than an elite football team, complaining about the artistic merit of a highly unlikely comeback win seems unnecessarily churlish, even if Matheus Cunha’s celebration of the winner was a little over the top. Roma managed to capitulate to Manchester United while being 2-0 up. Even Man Utd haven’t managed to do that too many times but I wouldn’t describe their second half performance as ‘ a comeback for the ages ’. Their opponents just didn’t turn up” – Nigel Sanders. These suggestions of paper and velcro shirts seem overly complicated. ( yesterday’s Football Daily letters ). If teams would just commit to using body paint instead of clothing, the foul becomes impossible to commit unless a defender is possessed of both long fingernails and a cavalier disregard for the health of their opponent. Also, no more tedious yellow cards for removing the shirt after a goal. Win win” – Ben Mimmack. Poor Nuno can take comfort that he’s in a long list of managers seen off by a poor result against West Brom since 2010, including Chris Hughton twice and five others. If you add Roberto di Matteo (he clung on for one more game) and spoiling Alex Ferguson’s leaving do with a 5-5 draw we were responsible for nine dismissals in seven years between 2010 and 2017. I think that’s pretty impressive. We’ve been quiet since then but perhaps we’re going for another run – championship managers beware” – Tom Levesley. Not bad for a 40-year-old whose physique is more like that of a wrestler than a whippet. “A few years ago, I feel like I could have definitely done sub-3:00,” he said, lamenting his late-career injuries for hindering him. Then came a reminder of the humble football’s extraordinary power to bend history, minds and wills. United’s players departed victorious having somehow won the game within the game, separating themselves from the fog of unhappy context swirling on all sides and turning the second half into its own soaring, ripping story for the ages. Will it be enough to save Michael Carrick, who was once again serenaded when minds wandered from the joint scourges of the Glazer family and Jim Ratcliffe? If Aston Villa defend a shade more competently than Roma on Sunday then perhaps not. United have led their supporters, remarkable in their tenor of backing for players and head coach here, up more than enough false peaks over the past 13 years. Arguably, that is one reason for Carrick being given the job on a permanent basis. Continue reading...

item.title: Unai Simón caps myth-making week with another extraordinary night | Sid Lowe
item.description: Athletic’s win over Real Sociedad was culmination of six unique days for the Spain keeper after night at the Palladium For the third time in six days everyone got to their feet to hand a standing ovation to Unai Simón, dressed in all black, before the world. Named the best men’s goalkeeper on the planet, holding the Lev Yashin trophy, they had applauded him at the London Palladium on Monday night and before the game began at San Mamés, Bilbao, on Sunday. Now somewhere in the middle of it all, the ferocity of the 197th Basque derby, there was another moment, even more meaningful and more lasting, a cheer again giving way to something deeper: an appreciation for a man as well as his work closing a week that will be forever his. Which means it will be forever theirs too. Real Sociedad and Athletic Club had been doing battle for 72 minutes and it was 2-1 when Simon took off to make a save that denied Carlos Soler an equaliser and defied belief . As the ball flew off his palm, San Mamés exploded. And then it happened: never mind that Athletic still had a derby to win and a corner to defend, forget the fact that the lead was a single goal, the visitors relentless now and 25 minutes still to resist; at the stadium everyone calls the Cathedral , a place of ritual and liturgy like no other, the entire congregation, 50,092 people, started clapping. Started and did not stop. For a minute, maybe more, it was like the match that matters most didn’t matter at all, momentarily fading until it was just him and them together. Continue reading...

item.title: Mourinho’s plan comes together as Real Madrid relaunch with clásico statement | Sid Lowe
item.description: It was just like old times as José Mourinho ended a night at Camp Nou with a knee slide and three points José Mourinho had already done the por qu é? , the printout and the press conference no-show in under 100 days. Now he’s done a knee slide too, and in the perfect place: back where it all began and where it can all begin again. When Kylian Mbappé scored the first in the clásico on Sunday night, Real Madrid’s manager hardly moved, sitting in the shadow of the bench – but when the striker got the second to win it with time running out, that was different. Mourinho leapt into the light, throwing himself to the grass, the knees of a 63-year-old’s trousers muddy as a schoolboy’s, stuck his tongue out and pumped his fists. He does so love it when a plan comes together. To the right of him, the bench was emptying, subs joining the players in sprinting towards the south-west corner. As they leapt about, dodging the bottles thrown towards them from the end, way, way up in the furthest corner and stuck inside a glass box like a bunch of David Blaines, the small group of Madrid fans who had come were going mad. In the main stand, a thousand phones were raised. And 600 kilometres west, back in Boadilla, Thibaut Courtois was watching his teammates from the sofa at home, presumably wrapped in a blanket and cradling a cup of Lemsip. On the morning of the biggest game there is, he awoke with flu, forced to miss out. Continue reading...

item.title: The horse that ushered in Manchester United’s tragic arc | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: There’s plenty of blame to go around at Old Trafford. Like all downfalls it started with a seemingly small, unconnected moment Sign up for our free newsletter here And so here we are again, at that point as the nights draw in and Manchester United prepare to sack a manager . Autumn: season of mists, mellow fruitfulness and a crisis at Old Trafford. Sunday’s 3-0 home defeat to Bournemouth , coming on the back of last week’s 4-1 reverse against Como, made clear what many had feared from the moment Michael Carrick was given the job on a permanent basis: that he isn’t up to it. But then, who could be? When you’ve burned through a long list of managers in 13 years, it’s perhaps worth considering whether the manager is really the problem. Could some blame perhaps go to the director of football, Jason Wilcox, or the chief executive, Omar Berrada, the people making the appointments? Or perhaps to Sir Jim Ratcliffe, the cost-cutting tax exile and minority shareholder with responsibility for sporting operations? Or to the Glazer family, who plunged the club into debt with a leveraged buyout in 2005 and have since made calamitous decision after calamitous decision, reducing the most successful club in English league history to a mid-table laughing stock with a roof that leaks symbolically ? item.title: James McClean: ‘Wearing the poppy was just never going to happen’
item.description: The former Republic of Ireland international on growing up in a community still reeling from the Troubles and the controversy that scarred his career “The perception of me is that, basically, I am a madman,” James McClean says calmly. “I’m outspoken. I’m a loudmouth. I’m very opinionated and I hate all things British. That’s from people who don’t know me. The reality is quite the opposite. I’m pretty boring. I go training, go home and switch off. A lot of my days are quite bland, quite basic.” McClean sounds as sane as he looks gaunt on a bleak Monday in Derry. He spent 14 years in English football and the fact that he is now at war with his own club, Derry City, can’t obscure the fact that he is the fifth-most-capped Republic of Ireland international, having played 103 times. “People define success in different ways,” he says, “but I’m the only footballer from the north of Ireland to win over 100 caps for Ireland. I played 150 Premier League games over five seasons, 800 professional games and won a lot of individual accolades. I count that as success and don’t look back with regrets.” Continue reading...

item.title: Next Generation 2021: why slow and steady sometimes wins the race
item.description: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future success Read the full updates on our class of 2021 here and here In 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series . We then follow these talented boys on their journeys for five years. Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well). The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players. The youngest to play in the Bundesliga at 16 years and one day, youngest player to appear in the Champions League 17 days later, youngest goal scorer in Bundesliga 11 days after that and youngest player and youngest goal scorer for the Germany Under-21 team before he has turned 17.
